Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Odisha: Konark, Bhubaneswar temples and Buddhist hills

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

Odisha has one UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Konark Sun Temple, inscribed in 1984. Around it lies one of India's densest heritage regions: Bhubaneswar's Kalinga-style temples from the 7th to 13th centuries, the Jain caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri, the Ashokan edict at Dhauli, the Buddhist sites of Ratnagiri, Lalitgiri and Udayagiri, and the fort of Sisupalgarh.

We arrange Odisha visits to Konark, Bhubaneswar and the Jain caves, with a Kalinga architecture lecture for your group before you go.

Why Odisha matters for Indian heritage

Ancient Kalinga was the land Ashoka conquered in a war that, by his own account in his edicts, filled him with remorse. Within two centuries the Jain king Kharavela was ruling from here and recording his deeds in the Hathigumpha inscription. Later, from about the 7th to the 13th century, Odisha developed a distinct temple style, now called Kalinga architecture, whose sequence can be followed almost temple by temple in Bhubaneswar.

For students this means one compact region covers Mauryan edicts, early Brahmi inscriptions, Jain rock-cut monasteries, Buddhist stupas and monasteries, and a complete temple tradition from its experiments to its peak at Konark. Our explainer on Ashoka and his edicts is useful background.

Museums in Odisha

  • Odisha State Museum, Bhubaneswar. Sculpture, palm-leaf manuscripts, coins and inscriptions.
  • ASI Site Museum, Konark. Sculpture recovered from the fallen parts of the Sun Temple.
  • ASI Site Museums, Ratnagiri and Lalitgiri. Buddha images and finds from the excavations.

Konark Sun Temple: Odisha's UNESCO site

Built in the 13th century under the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I, the Konark temple was designed as a colossal chariot for the sun god, with 24 carved wheels and seven horses. The great tower has fallen, and what stands today is the jagamohana (assembly hall), filled with sand by the British in the early 20th century to stop it collapsing. The sculpture on the platform and walls covers court life, music, war, animals and erotic scenes.

Plan at least half a day. Look at the wheels up close, then step back to see the hall's pyramidal roof and its tiers of musicians. Our session on Konark Sun Temple: architecture and astronomy explains the design and tests the popular claims about it against evidence.

Bhubaneswar: a temple sequence in one city

Bhubaneswar keeps temples from almost every stage of the Kalinga style. Parasurameswara (7th century) is early and compact. Mukteswara (10th century) is small and finely carved, with a famous torana. Rajarani, without a presiding deity today, is known for its sculpture of female figures. The Lingaraja, of the 11th century, is the mature form, a tall curved deul with a full set of halls. Non-Hindus may not enter the Lingaraja but can view it from a platform outside.

The city walk is best done with a guide who can point out how the rekha deul (curved tower) and pidha deul (stepped roof) change over time. See our Bhubaneswar heritage walk guide and the programme Bhubaneswar Ekamra: temples and urban sacred landscape.

Jain caves, Ashokan edicts and Buddhist hills

On the edge of Bhubaneswar, the twin hills of Udayagiri and Khandagiri hold rock-cut cells made for Jain monks around the 1st century BCE. The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela, in Brahmi script, is a key source for early Odishan history, and the two-storey Rani Gumpha has some of the liveliest relief carving of its time. Our Udayagiri and Khandagiri Jain heritage visit covers both hills.

At Dhauli, a rock carries a set of Ashoka's edicts, including the separate Kalinga edicts, beneath a carved elephant emerging from the stone. Further north, in Jajpur and Cuttack districts, Ratnagiri, Lalitgiri and Udayagiri form a Buddhist group with stupas, monasteries and fine Buddha images. Lalitgiri yielded relic caskets, and Ratnagiri's monastery is one of the best preserved in eastern India.

Puri, Chilika and other places

Puri's Jagannatha temple, of the 12th century, is a major pilgrimage centre and entry is restricted to Hindus, but the town's streets, mathas and the Rath Yatra route are part of its heritage. Sisupalgarh, on Bhubaneswar's outskirts, is an early historic fortified city with gateways visible in its earthen walls. Ranipur Jharial in western Odisha has a rare circular yogini temple, as does Hirapur near Bhubaneswar.

For a longer itinerary, our tour Temples of eastern India links Odisha with neighbouring regions.

Questions people ask

How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are in Odisha?

One. The Konark Sun Temple was inscribed in 1984. Odisha has many other important sites, including the Bhubaneswar temples, Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves, Dhauli and the Buddhist sites of Ratnagiri and Lalitgiri, but none of these is on the World Heritage List.

What is Kalinga architecture?

Kalinga architecture is the Odishan temple style, developed from about the 7th to the 13th century. A temple usually has a curved sanctum tower called the rekha deul and a hall with a stepped pyramidal roof called the pidha deul. Bhubaneswar shows its development and Konark its climax.

Which are the most important ancient temples in Odisha?

The Konark Sun Temple, the Lingaraja, Mukteswara, Parasurameswara and Rajarani temples in Bhubaneswar, and the Jagannatha temple in Puri. The yogini temples at Hirapur and Ranipur Jharial are rarer forms worth adding.

What is the Hathigumpha inscription?

It is a Brahmi inscription on the Udayagiri hill near Bhubaneswar recording the reign of the Jain king Kharavela of Kalinga, usually dated to about the 1st century BCE. It is one of the main sources for early Odishan history.

Can non-Hindus enter the Lingaraja and Puri temples?

No. Entry to the Lingaraja temple in Bhubaneswar and the Jagannatha temple in Puri is restricted to Hindus. At the Lingaraja a viewing platform outside the wall lets visitors see the tower.
